e: From the genus name, from Japanese アケビ (akebi).
Presumably from Japanese, and 木 (ki) is Japanese for tree, but no such Japanese word appears in reference works. Perhaps a scribal error for *asuhi, Japanese あすひ (asuhi, “Thujopsis dolabrata”).

From Middle English aketoun, aketon, from Old French aqueton, auqueton, alqueton, from Old Spanish alcoton (modern algodón), from Arabic الْقُطْن (al-quṭn), definite of قُطْن (quṭn, “cotton”). Doublet of cotton.
